page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8y.small is an entry-level memory-optimized instance built on the ARM64 architecture. Powered by Alibaba's custom YiTian710 processor operating at 2.75 GHz, this virtual machine provides 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU with no simultaneous multithreading. It features 8.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 64 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware-assisted AES cryptography support. The server includes no bundled local storage, contains 0 GPUs, and operates over a 1 Gbps baseline network interface under the KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark data reflects the resource boundaries of a single-core instance. In CPU assessments, the instance achieved an average stress-ng single-core score of 1762.39, while overall multi-core and PassMark CPU metrics placed in the bottom 10% due to the single-thread ceiling. Memory subsystem benchmarks recorded 101.6 GB/sec for small cached blocks, dropping to 18.26 GB/sec for large uncached read transfers and 7.15 GB/sec for large write operations. In workload-specific benchmarks, compression performance stayed within the middle 50% bracket with 27.47 GB/sec in gzip, whereas Redis recorded 1.46 million SET operations per second and static web throughput reached 1.63 GB/sec.

Cost efficiency for the ecs.r8y.small stems from its ARM architecture and dense memory-to-core ratio, providing 8.0 GB of memory without requiring payment for excess processing units. Tradeoffs focus on processing concurrency and input/output bandwidth, as compute-heavy tasks and multi-threaded scaling are constrained by the single core, and storage depends entirely on remote network-attached disks. The instance is best suited for low-traffic in-memory caches, lightweight Redis nodes, background utility tasks, microservices, and development environments that require substantial memory capacity relative to compute capacity.
